sections.h2: What does the Delaware County recorder do?
sections.html:
The Delaware County Recorder indexes every real estate and personal property record filed in the county, collects the filing fees, and keeps military service discharge records. For a home sale, that means the deed that moves title to the buyer and the mortgage release that clears the seller's lender both end up in this office.

The office is at 145 N. Union St., Delaware, OH 43015, phone (740) 833-2460. Recordings are taken Monday through Friday from 8:30 to 4:30, excluding holidays, and the document submission cutoff is 4:00 p.m. The recorder's home page also has a records search, a veterans graves search and a property fraud page.

sections.h2: How much does it cost to record a deed in Delaware County?
sections.html:
A basic deed or mortgage of up to two pages costs $39.00 at the Delaware County Recorder, plus $8.00 for each added page. The recorder's fee page marks the $39.00 as including a $5.00 preservation surcharge allowed under ORC 317.32.

Selected Delaware County recording charges (source: Delaware County Recorder, Fees and Charges page)
ItemCharge
Deed, mortgage, lease, release or assignment, 8.5 x 14 or smaller$39.00 for the first 2 pages, $8.00 each additional
Marginal reference (release, amendment, assignment, re-recording)$4.00 each
Photocopies$2.00 per page
Certified copies$2.00 per page plus $2.00 for certification
Federal tax lien release$3.00
Veteran's dischargeNo fee

The statute itself, ORC 317.32, builds the first-two-pages charge from a $17 base fee and a $17 housing trust fund fee, then $4 plus $4 for each later page, with an optional surcharge of up to $5 for document preservation. The office asks that documents sent by mail include a postage-paid return envelope or money to cover postage.

sections.h2: What happens between signing the deed and recording it in Delaware County?
sections.html:
The deed passes through the county auditor first and reaches the recorder second. Ohio's ORC 322.02 says any county real property transfer tax is paid by the grantor to the county auditor when the deed is delivered, before the deed goes to the recorder. The buyer's value statement under ORC 319.202 is filed with the auditor at the same stage.

  • Have the signed deed ready, along with the buyer's statement of value for the auditor, who endorses the deed.
  • Pay any transfer tax or conveyance charge the auditor collects. Ask the Delaware County Auditor at (740) 833-2900 for the current figure on the day of closing.
  • Carry the endorsed deed to the recorder before the 4:00 p.m. document cutoff, with the recording fee and a return envelope if it is being mailed back.
  • Check the recorder's online search afterward to confirm the deed and any mortgage release appear under the right parcel.

Most sellers never do these steps by hand, because the closing agent files the package. It still helps to know where each document sits, so you can ask the closing agent for the recording date.

sections.h2: What deed types does the Delaware County recorder define?
sections.html:
The recorder's Real Estate Recording page explains three common deeds in plain terms, using a standard real estate dictionary. A general warranty deed is one where the grantor agrees to protect the grantee against any other claim to title and makes other promises. A special warranty deed limits that promise to claims arising through the grantor, and the grantor does not warrant against defects that existed before they owned the land.

A quitclaim deed conveys only whatever rights the grantor has, without describing those rights and without warranties of ownership. The same page defines the grantor as the person giving the deed and the grantee as the buyer. Which form a sale uses is a contract and title company decision, and the recorder does not choose it.

sections.h2: What is Delaware County like beyond the courthouse?
sections.html:
Delaware County reached 242,032 residents in the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate, and the county covers 443 square miles of land north of Franklin County. QuickFacts lists 82,287 households for 2020 to 2024, and 89.4% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier.

Monthly owner costs tell the cost-of-ownership story: a median of $2,493 with a mortgage and $986 without, and median gross rent of $1,492. Workers spend 25.4 minutes on average getting to work. Delaware, the county seat, is also home to Ohio Wesleyan University, founded by Methodists in 1842, and Columbus State Community College opened a county campus in 2010. The Civil War era brought railroad business and technology to the county, per Wikipedia.

faqs.q: What does a two-page deed cost to record in Delaware County?
faqs.a: It costs $39.00, which includes the $5.00 preservation surcharge, per the recorder's fee page. Each additional page after the first two adds $8.00.

faqs.q: What is the document cutoff time at the Delaware County recorder?
faqs.a: The cutoff for document submission is 4:00 p.m., although the office takes recordings from 8:30 to 4:30 on weekdays. Holidays are excluded.

faqs.q: Does Delaware County charge to file a veteran's discharge?
faqs.a: No. The fee schedule lists a veteran's discharge, and an expunged discharge, as no fee.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer tax when a house is sold in Delaware County?
faqs.a: Under ORC 322.02, a county transfer tax is levied on the grantor named in the deed and paid to the auditor before the deed is recorded. Ask the auditor at (740) 833-2900 what rate is in effect.

faqs.q: Can I search Delaware County recorded documents online?
faqs.a: Yes. The recorder's site has a recorded document search page linked from its home page, and a separate search for veterans graves. Use it to confirm your deed or a mortgage release was recorded.
